comparator.sourceNotes: Checked 2026-11-13. Current BA-FIS retains revised years 1/2: 24 required 5 EC units = 120 EC. Adopted 2026–2027 OER 2.4/2.5 and 3.1/3.2 establish three years, 180 EC, 150 required plus 30 open EC. Footnote 17 distinguishes entrants before 2025; 3.2.3–3.2.6 govern level, approval and non-overlap, with Honours excluded. The revised diagram names six third-year spring units and explicitly weights Moot Court Tax Law at 5 EC. Retain 26 supported components totalling 155 EC, including genuine 30 EC open space; remaining 25 required EC lack a revised-cohort individual allocation. Current catalogue year 3 is explicitly for entrants in 2024 or earlier. Seven actual current module records provide useful 5 EC weights, specialist tax-law content, thesis and entry rules for that outgoing structure, but no explicit revised-cohort bridge. The forward-year request returns the same current record. OER 3.3.2 and 4.2.1 still delegate final-work standards and mandatory order to the guide. Do not infer equal revised weights, import the outgoing thesis or treat Moot Court as its replacement. Current curriculum overview and transition table do not establish that bridge. Existing verified 60 interest classifications and 18 current-UCR contribution findings remain relevant; no complete comparison, no-match or professional equivalence is inferred. LLP/tutoring/language-test placeholders add no credits. Stage2retainsall26documentedcomponents155EC andcurrentrevisedfirst24module5ECweights. FreshOERtextreadviawebretriever; reviseddiagramversionactuallyread13NovemberretainedwithoutfreshPDFclaim. Remaining25requiredEC/finalwork/progressionandexactnewMootCourtassessmentuncertified. Boundednegativeproofrests onconfirmedfirst120fiscal/legalintegration,notoutgoingthird-yearimports.

exception.reason: UCR offers substantial legal study, taxation policy, public economics, accounting and legal argumentation. Its strongest feasible combinations do not sustain the interpretation and application of fiscal legislation that the confirmed Leiden core already develops through income and payroll taxation, fiscal profit and VAT cases. Economic analysis of taxation and general legal methods provide real connections, but do not supply that integrated fiscal-law study. This judgment does not depend on professional qualification or Dutch-language teaching alone.
exception.curriculumContext: Revised legal foundations60EC and second-year fiscal/legal study60EC are confirmed. Open elective/minor space30EC is confirmed by currentOER and diagram. The third-year compulsory30EC outline covers fiscal administrative procedure, advanced formal tax law, direct taxesIIgeneral/advanced, international tax lawI and MootCourtTaxLaw; only MootCourt5EC is explicitly weighted in that diagram. Its relation to finalwork and the applicable course-level progression remain unresolved. No outgoing thesis or old15EC elective package is imported. Moot Court Tax Law5EC is now included as a supported requirement, without certifying final-work equivalence or entry conditions; remaining25EC of compulsory units await individual weights. audience.programmeDescription: Students examine taxation in law, business and society. They combine legal interpretation and argument with economics, accounting and ethics. Teaching is mainly in Dutch.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers law, accounting and study of taxation policy. The main gap is sustained study of tax legislation and its application to cases.

curriculum.limitation: Verified subset: 155 of 180 EC. Credits for the remaining 25 EC of advanced fiscal courses, the final-work requirement and third-year progression conditions still need confirmation for the revised curriculum. Moot Court is confirmed as 5 EC, but its relationship to final work is unresolved. The older third-year table cannot supply these details. Elective study must meet Leiden’s level and approval rules and avoid overlap with required courses.
